findings.location: lines 391-398, dynein-stalk-0 and dynein-stalk-1 lower ends; tubulin instanced geometry lines 147-189
findings.evidence: The shown dynein microtubule-binding stalks terminate at y=-0.42, z=+/-0.13 with radius 0.044. At 14 sampled planted-head states spanning the entire 10-event run, exact triangle closest-point/segment-triangle measurements on the rendered instanced tubulin surfaces give axis-to-surface distances 0.05166-0.08182. Subtracting a full stalk-radius envelope still leaves strictly positive clearances 0.00766-0.03782. At rest, both stalks are detached (clearance lower bounds 0.02471 and 0.01929). Existing tests verify stationary endpoints but never contact with tubulin. Full measurements: evidence/rna/diagnostic.json contacts[].
findings.whyWrong: Directional dynein transport needs a microtubule-bound supporting motor domain. The only displayed binding stalks remain visibly separated from the track while cargo translates, so the current geometry omits the actual mechanical connection and contradicts the depicted attached supporting foot. This is a geometric defect, not a complaint about schematic step sizes.
findings.fix: Give each dynein stalk a terminal microtubule-binding domain and/or align its planted tip with the actual tubulin surface, preserving continuous stalk-ring attachment, distinct dynein gait, backwards event, ATP branch and preallocated resources.
findings.verification: Regression must measure actual transformed binding-domain/stalk geometry against tubulin triangle surfaces throughout each planted interval and at rest/end, while the moving head detaches then returns. It should fail on current coordinates. Retain existing stationary-support, repeated-head, backwards-event, net-displacement, ATP and seek/resource checks.

continuity.checked: 401 samples for all 4 conditions, all floor/event transitions inspected, five interior samples per step in existing regression, and irregular repeated seeks.
findings: Position formulas join continuously at event boundaries; however planted-head spatial constancy is insufficient because actual stalk-track attachment fails (20261004-rna-01).
limits: Foot touchdown uses a sinusoidal lift with a velocity change at event boundaries; a ground-contact transition is not itself a confirmed position discontinuity. Integrator still needs continuous rendered playback.
